name: How Claude remembers your project
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26; no immutable documentation release declared. The page separately documents version-qualified features, including direct AGENTS.md support at v2.1.277+; do not treat the entire page as a v2.1.304 specification.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] CLAUDE.md and auto memory are model context, not enforced configuration. Managed settings and client permission rules are the technical enforcement layer.
Managed CLAUDE.md provides organization guidance but is distinct from managed permissions.deny, sandbox policy, and other client-enforced settings.

Ancestor and project instruction files concatenate into context rather than replacing each other; within a directory CLAUDE.local.md follows CLAUDE.md, and nested instructions load on relevant file access.
The recommendation to target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md is not a universal truncation limit. Imported content loads with its parent and still consumes context.
Use path-scoped .claude/rules files for file-specific guidance and skills for procedures that should not always occupy context.
Use /context to verify startup memory files; lazy nested files need not appear in that list. InstructionsLoaded hooks can record when and why instruction files load.

name: Settings files and precedence
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26; no fixed page version declared. General stack has key-specific, security, list, flag, and environment-variable exceptions documented on the page.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] User settings are ~/.claude/settings.json, team-shared settings are committed .claude/settings.json, personal project overrides are .claude/settings.local.json, and managed settings carry organization policy.

General precedence is managed settings > command-line --settings > project local > shared project > user. Environment variables and dedicated flags have per-key behavior rather than a universal position in that stack.
Lists such as permissions.allow merge across scopes rather than replacing each other. An allow saved locally does not outrank a project or managed ask rule.
allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly can constrain accepted permission rules to managed policy. Some security-sensitive keys preserve restrictive values from lower scopes.
Committed allow rules wait for interactive workspace trust, while deny and ask rules apply immediately. A repository-tracked settings.local.json also follows repository trust rules.
Claude Code excludes settings.local.json from git when it writes the file; manually created personal settings should be explicitly gitignored.
/status reports active setting sources, not per-key provenance. In -p mode broken settings or individual invalid values may be skipped without a dialog; documented managed-document exceptions apply.

name: Hooks reference
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26. onFailure: block requires v2.1.295+; documented per-hook timing lines require v2.1.296+. Agent hooks are explicitly experimental. Newer platform-specific details on the page are separately version-qualified.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] Command hooks run scripts at lifecycle events; prompt hooks call an LLM for a single-turn JSON decision; agent hooks can inspect files with tools and are experimental.

With plain or empty stdout, exit 0 succeeds, exit 2 blocks on block-capable events, and other nonzero exits normally report non-blocking errors. Valid JSON decision output and per-event exceptions affect this simplified rule.
PreToolUse exit 2 blocks a tool call. PostToolUse cannot undo the executed tool and returns feedback. Stop exit 2 continues the conversation. PermissionRequest has a separate decision contract.
A valid JSON blocking decision can block on exit 0. For ordinary non-fail-closed hooks, valid JSON can also be honored despite another nonzero exit, while exit 2 cannot be overridden by JSON allow.

For supported command/HTTP events, onFailure: block blocks on crashes, missing executables, invalid output, or timeouts. It has no effect on Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, or background command hooks.
Prompt hooks return ok and a reason when false; their effect depends on event and continueOnBlock. Prompt-hook ok:false has no effect on PermissionRequest.
async:true command hooks provide later feedback and cannot control the already-completed action through decision, permissionDecision, or continue.

Command hooks execute with full user access and outside the Bash sandbox. A -p/SDK session treats the folder as trusted for hooks in settings files, so review repository hooks or constrain automatic customization loading.
Debug details go to --debug-file or ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt. --debug does not print the debug log to the terminal.

name: Extend Claude with skills
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26. Ignoring non-managed skill grants under allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly is documented for v2.1.282+. Some page features require versions beyond local CLI 2.1.304, including added-directory command-name qualification in v2.1.309+ and doctor usage analysis in v2.1.305+.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] Normal skill discovery supplies names/descriptions; the SKILL.md body loads when invoked; linked supporting references load only when needed. Preloaded subagent skills are an exception to description-only startup.
disable-model-invocation:true makes a skill user-controlled and removes its description from the model listing; user-invocable:false hides direct user invocation while allowing model invocation.
Skill instructions can persist across turns, but allowed-tools pre-approval applies only to the invoking turn and clears on the next user message.

allowed-tools is a permission grant, not an exclusive list of available tools; other tools remain governed by ordinary permission settings. Managed-only permission policy can ignore non-managed skill grants.
The resolve-skills table identifies /review as a bundled alias of /code-review; a project code-review override does not replace the bundled alias.
The current page distinguishes interactive /doctor, which diagnoses and can propose confirmed fixes, from terminal claude doctor, which performs read-only installation diagnostics.

name: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26; no immutable page version declared. Managed-provided server precedence is documented for v2.1.259+; discovery-cache support for v2.1.221+; several other features are individually version/rollout-qualified.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] Verify that you trust an MCP server before connecting it; servers retrieving external content can expose the agent to prompt injection.
Project MCP configuration is shared through root .mcp.json. Local/project-private and user-wide MCP configuration live in ~/.claude.json, unlike general local settings in .claude/settings.local.json.

For duplicate ordinary server names, local scope outranks project and project outranks user; the entire server entry is selected, not field-merged. Managed-provided server definitions have separately documented higher priority.

Interactive sessions ask approval for project servers. -p and SDK sessions load them without that prompt. --strict-mcp-config selects only supplied MCP configuration, with managed MCP policy qualifications.
The PostgreSQL example explicitly recommends a read-only database user when queries must not modify data.
Added means configuration was saved, not that credentials or transport work. /mcp, claude mcp list, and claude mcp get expose connection/authentication/approval status.
A cached remote tool list can be available before a live connection; the server connects on first use. Failure details avoid expanded credential-bearing URLs.

name: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26; no immutable page version declared. Platform support and strict-mode behavior are qualified by the current page. Credential file masking is documented for v2.1.221+ with different Linux/WSL2 and macOS behavior.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] The OS-enforced Bash sandbox wraps shell commands and their child processes, not the whole Claude Code process.
Built-in file/web tools, command hooks, local MCP servers, and helper processes run outside that sandbox. Sandbox denyRead does not stop Read, and sandbox allowedDomains does not constrain WebFetch.

Default writes are limited to working directories and a per-user temporary directory, with protected configuration paths still denied. Reads remain broad and can include credential files; inherited environment secrets need explicit protection.
Network access passes through an allowed-domain proxy. Filesystem isolation and network isolation are separate controls.
Excluded commands and unsandboxed retries can leave the boundary. allowUnsandboxedCommands:false disables the retry but does not by itself eliminate excludedCommands.
By default an unavailable sandbox can result in unsandboxed execution; failIfUnavailable:true makes startup fail instead.

Credential deny/mask entries must be configured explicitly; the page states there is no built-in credential deny list. Enclosing containers/VMs can provide a broader boundary covering processes the Bash sandbox does not.

name: Run Claude Code programmatically
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26. --permission-prompts requires v2.1.259+; mcp_server_errors requires v2.1.219+. Manual is the documented unset -p starting mode on v2.1.302+. The page says bare mode is recommended now and a future -p default, not the current default.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] claude -p runs the agent non-interactively with text, JSON, or stream-json output; skills/custom commands can expand from the prompt.
Without bare mode, -p can discover repository/user customizations and run project settings hooks and MCP servers without showing workspace trust dialogs.

--bare skips automatic customizations and accepts explicitly supplied context/configuration. It does not read Anthropic subscription OAuth/keychain credentials; use ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper supplied through --settings. Third-party providers retain their own credential mechanisms.

--allowedTools auto-approves named tools rather than removing unlisted tools. Unlisted operations that need no approval can still run. dontAsk denies unresolved prompts, with documented mod/hook qualifications.
--permission-prompts none prevents waiting on an absent permission host; earlier permission rules, hooks, and the selected mode still decide calls first.

Run failures have a nonzero process exit; invalid flags are reported to stderr before execution, while failures inside a run can appear as results on stdout. structured_output is not guaranteed to be present if no valid structured result was produced.
system/init reports model/tools/plugins/MCP status. Invalid --mcp-config entries may be skipped while the run continues; mcp_server_errors and plugin_errors support explicit CI failure gates.
system/api_retry reports category, attempt, delay, and retry limit. JSON cost is an estimate and a resumed conversation's total includes preceding runs.

name: Claude Code GitHub Actions
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26. Examples target anthropics/claude-code-action@v1, a mutable major reference rather than a pinned action commit. Federation/app-permission claims describe the retrieved page, not a fixed July 2026 exam snapshot.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] Never commit API keys or OAuth tokens; put them in GitHub Secrets, grant only needed workflow permissions, and review Claude's changes before merging.

For organization-shared authentication, the page recommends a Console API key rather than a person's subscription OAuth token. It also documents service-account workload identity federation using GitHub OIDC to avoid a long-lived secret.

The official GitHub App serves multiple Claude products and has one combined permission set; GitHub does not allow arbitrary subset acceptance. The page describes a custom app when an organization needs only the action's narrower required set.
The action checks triggering write access and bot actors. GitHub/workflow permissions and model tool permissions are separate controls.
Use max-turns, workflow timeouts, and concurrency limits to bound automation; review examples separately grant only the tools needed to post findings.

Commits made through the default GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger subsequent workflows. The guide recommends GitHub App/custom app authentication and checking CI event triggers when Claude's commits do not start CI.

name: Best practices for Claude Code
section: Give Claude a way to verify its work
version: Rolling official recommendations retrieved 2026-10-26; no immutable page version declared. These are vendor workflow recommendations, not an independently measured productivity/quality benchmark.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] Give the agent runnable tests, build exits, lint checks, fixtures, or screenshots so it can evaluate and iterate on the result; require actual evidence rather than a success assertion.
Separate exploration and planning from implementation for uncertain or multi-file work, but skip planning overhead for small, clear changes.
Specify symptoms, relevant files, constraints, and acceptance conditions; the bug-fix examples call for a failing test reproducer and verification after the fix.
A writer/reviewer pattern uses a fresh session/context for review so the reviewer does not inherit the implementation reasoning; bundled /code-review also uses fresh subagent review context.
Scope reviews to correctness and stated requirements. A reviewer asked for gaps may report some even when code is sound, so do not blindly expand implementation to satisfy every stylistic suggestion.
Treat AI review as a second opinion alongside executable verification and existing human/CI controls; the page explicitly warns against shipping unverifiable plausible implementations.

name: Monitoring
version: Rolling official documentation retrieved 2026-10-26. Traces are labeled beta. Tool-result/tool-decision request_id and event agent ancestry fields require v2.1.310+, newer than the installed 2.1.304. Do not assume every documented field is present locally.
evidence: [COI: Anthropic; unverified independently; single-vendor evidence] OpenTelemetry needs CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 plus selected exporters and their endpoint/protocol configuration. Check claude_code.session.count for metrics or claude_code.user_prompt for logs-only export.
Third-party exporter failures appear as [3P telemetry] in the debug log; [Anthropic telemetry] belongs to a separate telemetry path.

api_request captures request duration/cost/tokens, api_error captures error/status/attempts, tool_result captures executed tools, and tool_decision captures permission decisions. Rejected calls do not emit tool_result.
prompt.id correlates the work initiated by one prompt; tool_use_id correlates tool events with hook input. request_id on tool_result/tool_decision requires v2.1.310+.
Beta distributed traces separate API time, tool permission wait, and tool execution; detailed hook spans require additional detailed-beta configuration beyond basic trace enablement.
Prompt and tool content/details are disabled by default, but standard attributes can include user.email and account/session identifiers. OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES can expose the whole conversation.

Repository settings cannot enable or redirect telemetry exporter variables. Configure the export through user/shell or managed settings; managed OTLP endpoint/credential settings remove conflicting developer destination variables as documented.
Telemetry/transcript joins and some correlation fields are version-sensitive, and trace content schemas include explicitly unstable detailed-beta attributes.
